title: The providers' app credentials, as the root broker keeps them
description: GET /api/v1/server/integrations lists the Google, Microsoft and Dropbox application sections of root's integrations file, the separate applications of the narrower account levels (microsoft_nosend, microsoft_drafts, microsoft_read, dropbox_app_folder), the multi-tenant Microsoft applications (microsoft_shared and its levels) and the organisations they are allowed to serve, with root's browser_setup switch. POST /api/v1/server/integrations/set {provider, fields} has the broker write one provider's section; POST /api/v1/server/integrations/clear {provider} removes it. POST /api/v1/server/integrations/tenants/set {tenant_id, label} adds an organisation to the allowed list or relabels it in place; POST /api/v1/server/integrations/tenants/remove {tenant_id} takes it off, which stops its connections on this server at their next use and deletes and revokes nothing (adding it back resumes them). A secret is accepted only in a set request and is never returned. A change is in effect only when the reply arrives; 503 outcome_uncertain means it may or may not have been written, and nothing is retried. Refusals are fixed codes shared with root's admin integrations CLI: browser_setup_disabled (root's switch is off), host_busy (host maintenance holds the lock; nothing was written), integrations_file_invalid (root must repair the file, including an allowed list the daemons refuse), integration_tenants_full (the list already has 32 organisations), integration_refused, broker_unavailable. Administrator, session and CSRF are required.

provider.description: A section: a provider's own application, which is its full account level, or the application of one of its narrower levels. The microsoft_shared sections are the operator's multi-tenant applications, one per level, serving the allowed organisations at every level no single-tenant section of that organisation fills.

tenant_id.description: A Microsoft Directory (tenant) ID, a GUID. Lowercase in every reply; a request may use either case.

label.description: The organisation's name as people on this server see it, 1 to 64 printable characters without a space at either end. Every person on the server can read it.

tenant.description: One organisation the shared Microsoft applications may serve, in the file's order. The list governs what this server's own connect, refresh and tool paths do; it is not a security boundary, because a sign-in with a multi-tenant application can be used by the person's own programs against any organisation that approved the application.

source.description: site_admin: the broker set exactly this label for actor at at; operator: root wrote or changed it.

actor.description: The administrator's GitHub id or root, as the gateway reported it.

client_id.description: Public: it is in every sign-in URL. Absent when root's hand-written value is not token-shaped.

tenant_id.description: Microsoft sections only: a single-tenant section's organisation, its Directory (tenant) ID and only sign-in authority; a shared section's owning tenant, which is never a sign-in authority on its own account. Shown as root wrote it, so an unusable hand-written audience keyword is visible.

usable.description: Whether every person's daemon uses this section; false sections are ignored there.

source.description: site_admin: the broker wrote exactly these bytes for actor at at; operator: root wrote or changed them.

actor.description: The administrator's GitHub id or root, as the gateway reported it.

browser_setup.description: Root's site.json integrations.browser_setup as host apply published it; while false, set and clear are refused.

tenants.description: The allowed organisations of the shared Microsoft applications. Empty when there is no list.

tenants_invalid.description: Present, and true, when root's list is one every daemon refuses whole (a key that is not a GUID, a label out of bounds, the same tenant twice or more than 32 entries); tenants is then empty, no organisation is served through the shared applications, and only root can repair it.

fields.description: Exactly the provider's fields: google, dropbox and dropbox_app_folder client_id and client_secret; every Microsoft section client_id and tenant_id. A Google client id ends in .apps.googleusercontent.com, both Microsoft ids are GUIDs (the tenant is a Directory (tenant) ID, never common, organizations or consumers: a single-tenant section's organisation, a shared section's owning tenant), and no value may be given twice.
